# Radial centering across families: exact covariance and a rate-slice obstruction

This is a concrete follow-up to
`candidate faf22898d0dc8331`.
The centered radial body preserves all halfspace masses THROUGH its
chosen center. It need not preserve the anchored convex-family inclusions
needed by mixed-integer geometry. The following obstruction occurs even
when the selected centers already agree exactly.

## 1. Exact covariance on pointed homothetic density families

Let f be a bounded, compactly supported log-concave density in R^r, of
mass W, and choose a radial-centering point c for f. Thus the radial body
L_{f,c}, defined by

    rho_(f,c)(u)^r=r integral_0^infinity t^(r-1) f(c+tu)dt,

is a convex body with centroid zero and volume W. For any a,s>0 and
b in R^r, set

    f_(a,s,b)(x)=a f((x-b)/s),    c_(a,s,b)=b+s c.

Changing variables t=s tau in the radial integral gives EXACTLY

    L_(f_(a,s,b),c_(a,s,b)) = a^(1/r) s L_(f,c),           (1)
    mass(f_(a,s,b))=a s^r W.                              (2)

In particular these specified centers remain radial-centering points.
This does not require uniqueness of the fixed point or of any general
log-concave deepest point.

Consequently there is a positive compatible-family statement. Suppose
bases z carry such densities with parameters (a_z,s_z,b_z), and at every
anchored integer-output convex representation z=sum theta_i z_i one has

    c_z=b_z+s_z c=sum_i theta_i c_zi,
    R_z=a_z^(1/r)s_z >=sum_i theta_i R_zi.                 (3)

Then the pointed radial bodies c_z+R_z L_(f,c) satisfy all the actual
Minkowski inclusions at integer outputs, have the exact original masses,
and preserve every halfspace mass through their own chosen center.
Indeed the Minkowski sum is c_z+(sum theta_i R_zi)L_(f,c), which lies in
the displayed body because zero belongs to L_(f,c). This is an exact
sufficient statement with both required compatibilities explicit.
It does NOT say that original cross-measure BM forces (3).

## 2. Genuine projected uniform homotheties have the wrong radial power

Let Q be a full-dimensional N-dimensional convex body, and project its
uniform volume onto an r-dimensional subspace, where 1<=r<N. Denote
its projected density by f. The projected density of sQ is

    f_s(x)=s^(N-r) f(x/s).                                (4)

Use the centering point sc for f_s. Formula (1) gives

    L_(f_s,sc)=s^(N/r)L_(f,c).                            (5)

The original family s_z Q is convex-compatible whenever s_z is positive
and concave at anchored representations. Yet a positive nonconstant
AFFINE radius s_z on a three-site chain has

    s_0=(s_-+s_+)/2,
    s_0^(N/r)<[s_-^(N/r)+s_+^(N/r)]/2.                   (6)

Thus the radial bodies fail midpoint inclusion strictly. When c=0 their
physical marks all coincide, so no affine-centering repair can fix this
failure. It comes from preserving N-dimensional source mass using
r-dimensional ordinary volume, which forces the power N/r>1.
A common scalar renormalization of all fibers does not change (6).

## 3. An exact N=2, r=1 three-fiber example

Take integer bases P={-1,0,1}, fix 0<t<1, and set s_z=1+t z.
The actual full-dimensional continuous fibers

    Q_z=[-s_z,s_z]^2

are the integer fibers of a convex body over [-1,1]; both pairs of
opposite side inequalities are affine in z. Their first-coordinate
projected measures have density

    f_z(x)=2s_z 1_[-s_z,s_z](x),   W_z=4s_z^2.             (7)

Each f_z is log-concave, its unique radial-centering point is c_z=0,
and its exact one-dimensional radial body is

    L_z=[-2s_z^2,2s_z^2].                                 (8)

The radial body at zero has endpoint 2. The endpoint Minkowski midpoint
has endpoint

    [(2(1-t)^2)+(2(1+t)^2)]/2=2(1+t^2)>2.                 (9)

The inclusion defect is exactly 2t^2 on EACH side. At t=1/2 the three
original masses are 1,4,9; the three radial intervals are
[-1/2,1/2], [-2,2], and [-9/2,9/2]. Their endpoint midpoint is
[-5/2,5/2], strictly outside the middle interval.

The centers satisfy every anchored representation, and all densities
are even. Their individual halfspace-depth fraction is exactly 1/2.
Neither center drift, different tangent spaces, failure of lattice
completeness, nor a noncritical source mark is responsible for (9).
The family is a direct marginal of one actual convex uniform family
with a common normalization and joint N=2 measure BM.

## 4. The same limit comes from ONE actual positive-rate coarea slice

The example can retain the precise common-coarea and rank-drop structure
of the current single-cell rate notes. Fix t=1/2, so

    S=sum_(z=-1,0,1) s_z^2=7/2.

For integer j>=12 put epsilon_j=1/(4jS)=1/(14j). In continuous
coordinates (x,u,v), form the actual full-dimensional compact convex body

    D_j={-1<=z<=1,
         |x|<=s_z, |u|<=epsilon_j s_z, 0<=v<=epsilon_j}.

Its defining inequalities are affine. Every body lies in one fixed
compact set and has the exact integer bases P. The total mixed
THREE-dimensional volume is

    M_j=sum_z 4epsilon_j^2 s_z^2=4epsilon_j^2 S.

Use the ONE global affine plane and rate data

    A_j(z,x,u,v)=v+exp(-2j)>0,
    lambda_j=j, s_j^rate=exp(-j), |c_j|=1.

The level is strictly inside the vertical slab: exp(j)>14j for j>=12,
for example by the cubic exponential term. Its actual normalized
coarea factor is

    alpha_j=1/(M_j lambda_j |c_j|)=1/epsilon_j.            (10)

At base z the level slice has |x|<=s_z and |u|<=epsilon_j s_z.
Multiplying its ordinary two-volume by alpha_j and letting j tend to
infinity yields the finite weak limit

    d mu_z(x,u,v)=2s_z 1_[-s_z,s_z](x) dx delta_0(u)delta_0(v).

These are exactly (7), supported in dimension q=1<N=2. The normalization
in (10) is ONE scalar common to every base, and the slices come from
one global affine cell. Thus neither a separately normalized fiber nor
an arbitrary projected law was substituted. This is a structural rate
example, not a canonical minimizing or full critical-cap-law example.

## 5. The normalization that repairs shape changes mass

There is an exact way to undo the radius power, but it does not preserve
the source measure. In the family (4), dilating the radial body by

    s^(-(N-r)/r)

changes its scale from s^(N/r) to s. Its volume becomes s^r W instead
of the original s^N W, so one must attach the variable density weight
s^(N-r) to restore cap masses. Ordinary UNWEIGHTED mixed volume no
longer represents the original family. The missing weight cannot be
ignored in a numerical cap payment.

Equivalently, normalization by the appropriate power of W_z replaces
source masses W_z by their r/N powers, up to one common constant. It
can restore a concave radius but destroys the additive original-volume
budget. Adding auxiliary continuous dimensions can restore the mass,
but then this step alone has not reduced the continuous dimension.

The positive message is exactly (1)-(3): pointed homothetic covariance
is available, with a fully explicit condition for compatible radial
bodies. The negative message is (5)-(10): even the actual single-cell
rank-drop hypotheses do not supply that condition, already in the
simplest symmetric three-fiber model.

## 6. Mass-root normalization fails on a nonhomothetic compatible family

Consider precisely the mass normalization suggested to repair Section 2:

    Lhat_z=W_z^(1/N-1/r) L_z.                            (11)

Its r-volume is W_z^(r/N). Appending a centered unit-volume cube in
N-r coordinates at radius W_z^(1/N) restores the exact original mass:

    J_z=Lhat_z x (W_z^(1/N)[-1/2,1/2]^(N-r)),
    |J_z|=W_z.                                           (12)

This fixes all pointed homothetic families satisfying the corresponding
center condition. But it fails for the following exact nonhomothetic
marginals of a compatible convex family.

Take N=3,r=2 and P={-1,0,1}. Let

    K_-=[-4,4] x [-1,1],
    K_+=[-1,1] x [-4,4],
    K_0=[-5/2,5/2]^2,
    Q_z=K_z x [-1/2,1/2].                                (13)

The original three-dimensional bodies satisfy

    Q_0=(Q_-+Q_+)/2.

They are the exact integer fibers of one convex body: over real
-1<=z<=1 use rectangular half-widths 5/2-3z/2 and 5/2+3z/2, with the
third width fixed. Projecting onto the first two coordinates gives
f_z=1_Kz and source masses

    W_-=W_+=16,    W_0=25.

All selected radial centers are uniquely zero, and the raw radial
bodies are exactly L_z=K_z. After (11), however,

    (Lhat_-+Lhat_+)/2=16^(-1/6) K_0,
    Lhat_0=25^(-1/6) K_0.                                (14)

The first body STRICTLY contains the second because 16<25. Thus
midpoint inclusion fails. For example the point

    (5/2)16^(-1/6) e_1

belongs to the endpoint Minkowski midpoint but is outside Lhat_0.
All original vertices and source masses are rational; the comparison
in (14) is an exact strict inequality of positive sixth powers.

Importantly, NO CHOICE of appended coordinates can repair (14) while
retaining the prescribed Lhat_z as their exact projections. Any
Minkowski inclusion J_0 superseteq (J_-+J_+)/2 projects to the missing
inclusion for Lhat. Thus the obstruction is stronger than a failure
of the particular product appendage (12). A different construction
would have to change the normalized projected bodies themselves.

This example has the opposite defect from Section 2: the unnormalized
radial bodies are already perfectly compatible, while the mass-root
normalization destroys their shape compatibility. All centers and
all tangent planes agree; no center selection can repair it.

## 7. The normalized-shape obstruction also has a true rate-slice realization

Continue with (13) and put S=16+25+16=57. For j>=12 set
 epsilon_j=1/(Sj). In continuous coordinates (x_1,x_2,u,v) use

    D_j={-1<=z<=1,
         |x_1|<=5/2-3z/2, |x_2|<=5/2+3z/2,
         |u|<=epsilon_j/2, 0<=v<=epsilon_j}.

This is a full-dimensional compact convex body with the exact three
integer fibers and one common compact bound. Its mixed FOUR-volume is

    M_j=epsilon_j^2 S.

Again take A_j=v+exp(-2j), lambda_j=j, and level exp(-j). The level
is inside the slab for j>=12: the fourth term of the exponential
series gives exp(j)>j^4/24>57j. The common normalization is exactly

    1/(M_j lambda_j |c_j|)=1/epsilon_j.

The normalized THREE-dimensional level slices converge to

    mu_z=1_Kz(x) dx delta_0(u)delta_0(v).

These retain N=3 and physical support rank q=2<N, and are precisely
the marginals in Section 6. Hence even actual single-global-cell
positive-rate geometry does not force compatibility of the
mass-normalized radial bodies or of an auxiliary lift retaining them
as its prescribed projections.
